new: pH 9.00 → pOH 5.00 → [OH−] = 1.0×10−5 M, so Q = (0.010)(1.0×10−5)2 = 1.0×10−12 for every metal. Only Mn(OH)2 (Ksp = 1.9×10−13) has Ksp < Q and precipitates. Mg(OH)2 (5.6×10−12) is the near miss: Q is still below its Ksp. Forgetting to square [OH−] gives Q = 1.0×10−7, which would wrongly precipitate Mg(OH)2 as well.
why: Without squaring, Q = 1.0e-7 exceeds only the Ksp of Mg(OH)2 (5.6e-12) and Mn(OH)2 (1.9e-13); Ca(OH)2 (5.0e-6) and Ba(OH)2 (2.6e-4) still exceed Q. So two would precipitate, only one wrongly, not three.
